facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Accordingly, work was started at Hastinapura in November 1950 and continued till March 1951... resumed at Hastinapura and finally closed in March 1952.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India conducted excavations under B. B. Lal at the ancient mound of Hastinapur between 1950 and 1952.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The excavation revealed that the site was occupied in five different periods, with a break between each.
facts.text: Excavations at Hastinapur established an occupational sequence of five distinct cultural periods separated by settlement gaps.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The first occupational slab ranging from Pre 1200 BC represent Ochre-coloured ware (OCW), there is no any structural remains found from this period because the area of excavation is limited.
facts.text: Period I at Hastinapur yielded a thin occupation containing Ochre Coloured Pottery dating to before 1200 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: B.B. Lal, the excavator of this site, gave a time bracket of 1100 BCE and 800 BCE to this pottery based on its stratigraphic position.
facts.text: Period II at Hastinapur was defined by the presence of Painted Grey Ware, dated by the excavator between 1100 BCE and 800 BCE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Mention may also be made of the presence of the horse (Equus caballus) during this Period... In a pit of this Period were found charred grains identified as rice.
facts.text: Excavations in Period II uncovered mud-plastered walls, copper tools, charred rice, and bones of the domesticated horse.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The occupation came to an end because of a heavy flood in the Ganga which washed away a considerable portion of the settlement. Signs of this devastation are left on the mound in the form of an erosional scar.
facts.text: The Painted Grey Ware occupation at Hastinapur was brought to an end by a massive flood of the Ganga dated to approximately 800 BCE.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Nichakshu, when Hastinapur is washed away by the Ganges, will remove his residence to Kausambi.
facts.text: Puranic dynastic chronicles describe King Nichakshu as the fifth reigning monarch in direct descent from King Parikshit.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The occurrence of PGW at Kausambi in period 2 also supports the literary tradition that the capital was shifted to Kausambi after the flood.
facts.text: Archaeological excavations at Kaushambi confirmed the emergence of a late phase of Painted Grey Ware that followed the timeline of Hastinapur's flood.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: This assessment by Lal ignited debates, which had put this pottery on the pedestal... scholars debate how closely the PGW cultural horizon corresponds to epic descriptions.
facts.text: While B. B. Lal argued that Painted Grey Ware represents the material culture of the Mahabharata epic due to its presence at traditional epic sites, skeptical historians argue that simple mud-brick agro-pastoral settlements lack the architectural grandeur of the text and cannot be linked to literary lineages without contemporary inscriptions.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: On the bank of the Budhi Ganga, two places near Hastinapur (Draupadi Ghat and Karna Ghat) reference Mahabharata personages.
facts.text: Local oral tradition identifies existing riverside mounds near the old river channel as sacred sites of the Pandavas, including the Pandeshwar temple and Draupadi Ghat.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: At present, the Ganga flows at a distance of about 8 kilometres from the site, but, in ancient times, it flowed much nearer.
facts.text: The main stream of the river Ganga currently flows approximately 8 kilometres east of the excavated site at Hastinapur.

visual.prompt: Doodle-style panel: a small old temple on a riverside mound with steps leading down to a narrow quiet stream, pilgrims seen from behind lighting lamps at the ghat, sunset reflections, peaceful mood, no text

scenes.vo: Pandeshwar mandir ko log Pandavon se jodte hain. Budhi Ganga ke kinare Draupadi Ghat aur Karna Ghat hain. Budhi Ganga yaani Ganga ki purani dhaara, jo ab patli reh gayi hai. Shaam ko yahan baithiye, purani nadi ki khamoshi sunaai degi.

scenes.label: archaeology

visual.prompt: Doodle-style panel: a lone visitor seen from behind standing on top of a grassy mound, gazing toward a distant silver river on the horizon across green fields, wind in the grass, reflective mood, no text

scenes.vo: Aur jab aap tile par khade hon, toh nadi ki taraf dekhiye. Woh door hai, par kabhi yahin thi. Wahi nadi jo granth mein bhi hai, aur mitti mein bhi. Shayad Hastinapur ki asli kahani yahi hai. Shehar aur nadi ka rishta.

scenes.label: disputed

visual.prompt: thinking

scenes.vo: Toh tasveer kuch aisi hai. Granth kehta hai, Ganga ne Hastinapur bahaaya. Mitti kehti hai, Ganga ne PGW basti bahaayi. Kuch vidwaan kehte hain, yeh wahi yaad hai. Kuch kehte hain, jodna abhi jaldi hai. Faisla sabut karega, aur sabut abhi adhoora hai.

scenes.label: scripture

visual.prompt: Doodle-style panel: high earthen ramparts of an ancient city rising beside a broad river at dawn, a lone traveller with a backpack seen from behind walking toward them, inviting adventurous mood, no text

scenes.vo: Agli baar hum chalenge Kausambi. Woh shehar jahan granth ke hisaab se raja Nichakshu pahunche. Wahan ki deewarein, wahan ke bartan, aur wahan ki mitti kya kehti hai. Sab kuch sabut ke saath, aur dono paksh ke saath.

visual.prompt: end_smile

scenes.vo: Ab aapki baari. Hastinapur ki baadh, granth ki yaad hai ya sirf sanyog? Comment mein bas likhiye, yaad ya sanyog. Aur agar aap kabhi Hastinapur gaye hain, toh bataiye wahan sabse pehle kya dekha.
